Fingertips are around 10 mm wide. Apple and Material both recommend about 44pt or 48dp targets; below that, mis-taps rise.
Make tappable areas at least 44 by 44 CSS pixels, using padding if the icon is small.
Rely on 16px icons as the hit area.
Adjacent small buttons invite the wrong tap. Gaps of 8px or more reduce errors.
Leave at least 8px between touch targets.
Pack actions into a dense row.
The OS reserves edge swipes for back and home. A carousel or drawer that needs the same swipe will fight it.
Keep custom swipes away from the screen edge and give buttons as an alternative.
Older mobile browsers waited before treating a tap as a click. touch-action:manipulation disables double-tap zoom on controls and removes the delay.
Apply touch-action:manipulation to buttons and links.
Pull to Refresh Does Not Fight Scroll
Custom pull gestures can collide with the browser's own refresh. Limit them to lists where it makes sense and keep a visible refresh button.
Use overscroll-behavior to manage chaining and offer a button.
Reimplement refresh on the whole page.
Vibration confirms an action for some people, but it is unsupported on many devices and annoying when overused.
Feature-detect navigator.vibrate and use it only for key confirmations.
Rely on vibration as the only feedback.
Place Key Actions Within Thumb Reach
On large phones the top corners are hard to reach one-handed. Primary actions fit better in the lower half.
Put the main action in a bottom bar or lower section.
Hide the main action in the top corner.
Hover Effects Do Not Hide Information
Touch devices have no hover, so content revealed only on hover is unreachable. Gate hover styling by capability.
Use @media (hover:hover) for hover polish and show the content by default.
Reveal prices or menus only on hover.
Long Press Needs a Visible Alternative
Hidden long-press menus are undiscoverable. Offer the same options in a visible overflow menu.
Expose the same actions through a labelled menu button.
Offer an action only on long press.
Hover Is Not the Only Cue
Hover states help mouse users, but must be paired with focus and active states for keyboard and touch.
A control that does not react on press feels broken. A short visual change confirms the input registered.
Style :active with a small shift or tone change within 100ms.
Give no feedback until the action finishes.
A disabled button leaves people unsure what to do. Where possible keep it focusable with aria-disabled and say what is missing.
Use aria-disabled and a hint, or let it submit and report.
Grey out a button with no reason.
Without feedback, people press again. A pending label and busy state show the request is in flight.
Change the label ('Saving'), set aria-busy, and keep the width stable.
A delete confirmation catches slips that cannot be undone. Name the item and the consequence in the dialog and on the button.
Use a dialog that restates what will go and a button labelled Delete invoice.
Use OK and Cancel with a vague prompt.
For reversible actions, confirm dialogs interrupt every time. A short undo window is faster and safer.
Apply the action and show an Undo in a status message for several seconds.
Pointer Cursor on Real Controls Only
cursor:pointer signals clickable. Applying it to non-interactive cards or text misleads.
Set cursor:pointer on links and buttons; leave static content alone.
Make an entire non-clickable card show a hand.
A setting that takes effect immediately is a switch. role='switch' with aria-checked tells assistive tech so.
Use input checkbox with role='switch' or a button with aria-checked.
Use a styled div with no state.
Whole Card Click Keeps One Link
Making a whole card clickable with nested links yields duplicate tab stops. One real link stretched over the card is cleaner.
Put one anchor on the heading and stretch its hit area with ::after.
Wrap the card in a link containing other links.
Disabling selection on content stops people copying addresses, codes and quotes.
Disable user-select only on controls and drag handles.
A skeleton in the shape of the content gives structure while it loads and avoids layout jumps; a lone spinner gives nothing.
Use skeletons for content areas and spinners only for short, unknown waits under a second.
Show a blank page until everything arrives.
Empty States Say What to Do
An empty list is a chance to explain and offer a first step, in plain words.
Say what belongs here and give one action to add it.
Leave an empty box or write 'No data'.
No bookings yet. Add the first one
Uploads, checkouts and imports feel faster when people see the step and how many remain.
Show 'Step 2 of 4' and a progress element with a label.
A message that disappears in two seconds is gone before it is read, or before a screen reader finishes. Allow time and a way to dismiss.
Show messages at least five seconds, pause on hover and focus, and keep them in a status region.
Use auto-dismiss under three seconds for anything important.
'Failed to load' leaves people stranded. Tell them what happened and offer retry, a different route or contact details.
Name the problem, show a retry button and keep their work.
Show a stack trace or a dead end.
'Done' is vague. State what happened and what comes next, such as when to expect a call.
Say what was saved, sent or booked, with a time or reference.
Booked for Tue 12 May, 9:30. We will text a reminder.
Phones lose signal. Telling people the app is offline and what still works beats silent failures.
Listen for the offline event and show a banner; queue writes where possible.
Let requests fail without a message.
Showing the result at once feels fast, but if the server refuses, the user must be told and the view restored.
Update the UI, and on failure revert and explain.
